reason: The mechanism is real - shell() at lately.html:724-728 prints 'Read at ${D.readingLong}' and a hard-coded 'Twelve weeks' for all seven states - but the finding is factually wrong about two of the three states it indicts, and the severity is overstated by two classes. EMPTY: the finding says 'the surface states the scope of a reading that never happened.' It did happen. SOURCES.empty is { tasks: 'answered, nothing recorded' }, and the coverage strip in the frame reads TASKS ANSWERED, NOTHING RECORDED. Tasks was asked, at 09:14, over twelve weeks, and returned no records. 'Read at 09:14' and 'Twelve weeks' are both literally true there; that is the honest-degradation contract working, not breaching. ERROR: the finding claims the header 'still says Read at 09:14 ... the same instant the card below calls the last good reading' as if that were a contradiction. Both strings are the same accessor, D.readingLong, and the fixture holds exactly one reading instant. The header is not asserting a fresh successful read at a time the card denies - it is the last good reading printed once at the top, which is precisely what the behaviour gate's 'unanchored time' block (interaction-check.mjs:336-350) exists to require in the error state. Ambiguous wording, not an untruth. FIRST-RUN: this is the one live sub-claim, and it is weaker than stated. 'Twelve weeks' reads as the window of the view - the lookback the Lately tab performs - not as a claim that twelve weeks of records exist; a 'Last 12 weeks' range label over a sparse series is standard at every named benchmark. And the state does not draw eleven zeros: the plot contains a baseline and one centred column, no gridlines, no eleven empty slots, so nothing fabricates the zero the contract forbids. The card then names the account's age twice in the reader's own words - '12 jobs finished since you started' and 'Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing. Yours arrive on 10 August.' The 'you did nothing for nearly three months' inference has to survive both of those, on the same card, to land. The declared class is 'misleading = the product asserts something untrue'; nothing here is untrue. At most this is a refinement in the header's precision on one of seven states. THE FIX IS ALSO WRONG AGAINST THE SOURCE. 'Derive the scope label from the weeks actually drawn, in the same one-accessor discipline as every other fact' cannot be done from D: D.weeks is F.weeks, always twelve entries in every state including first-run and empty - first-run is a presentational branch that renders D.weeks[11] alone (lately.html:781). There is no drawnWeeks to read. And the error half of the fix makes the surface worse: 'Asked at 09:14' beside 'Last good reading - 09:14' would assert that the failed request and the last success happened at the same instant, manufacturing the contradiction the finding wrongly claims already exists. Correct problem, wrong fix, wrong class - refuted, with the salvageable part sharpened below.
sharpenedFix: Do not derive a count. Declare scope per state in the table that already exists for exactly this purpose - add a SCOPE sibling to SOURCES (lately.html:696-703): full/partial/quiet/loading 'Twelve weeks'; first-run 'Since you started' (matching the hero's own words, keeping the slot a word rather than mixing 'Twelve' with a numeral '1'); empty and error null. Render the .reading label only when SCOPE[state] is non-null. Leave 'Read at' exactly as it is in all seven states: on empty the read genuinely happened, and on error it is the last good reading the card names, which the gate requires to be present. If the error header's 'Read at' still reads too confident, the only safe change is to qualify it with the same words the card uses - 'Last read at' - never to invent a second, different instant.
breaks: A null .reading on empty and error removes the header rule and the top block's third line, so the header's bottom margin and the first card's top offset change on two states - re-shoot light and dark empty and error at 1440x960 and 390x844 and re-run the asset gate on frame bytes. It also removes one of the three occurrences of D.readingLong on those states; interaction-check.mjs:336-350 only runs its anchor assertion on full/partial/quiet/first-run/error, and on error the card and the coverage strip still carry the instant, so it holds at anchored >= 2 - but that assertion is now load-bearing for a line the header no longer prints, so re-run the behaviour gate rather than assuming. 'Since you started' on first-run is longer than 'Twelve weeks' and sits at the flex end of a wrap container; check it does not wrap the rule to a second line at 390. audit.mjs is unaffected (no new hue, weight, family or size).
